long_biography.plain_text:
Jim Simons helped build Stony Brook's mathematics department by recruiting researchers including James Ax and Jeff Cheeger. His own collaboration with Shiing-Shen Chern produced geometric ideas that later became important tools in theoretical physics. He continued mathematical research after leaving full-time investment management, working on joint papers with Dennis Sullivan.

Through Math for America, which he founded in 2004, Simons also supported teachers' professional development. The organisation moved from recruiting new mathematics teachers towards retaining experienced teachers across science and mathematics. Its fellowships combine financial stipends with opportunities for teachers to exchange ideas and deepen their knowledge of the subjects they teach.
